title: bug: SourceCache limits parameter is typed as the frozen literal defaults, so custom limits do not compile
description: packages/moe-daemon/src/context/sourceCache.ts types the constructor's limits as Partial<typeof SOURCE_CACHE_LIMITS>. Object.freeze infers the literal types 2048 and 33554432, so `new SourceCache({ maxEntries: 1 })` fails tsc with TS2322 "Type '1' is not assignable to type '2048'". The tests only pass because tsconfig excludes *.test.ts, and C11's daemon wiring couldn't pass custom limits without a cast. Fix: type the limits as `{ maxEntries: number; maxBytes: number }`.
definitionOfDone: `new SourceCache({ maxEntries: 1, maxBytes: 10 })` typechecks under `npx tsc --noEmit` from non-test code (or a test file included in a typecheck)
Existing runtime validation of limits unchanged; `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` exits 0

implementationPlan.description:
Widen the SourceCache limit types (packages/moe-daemon/src/context/sourceCache.ts) and prove it in the tests.

(a) In sourceCache.ts:
- Add `export interface SourceCacheLimits { readonly maxEntries: number; readonly maxBytes: number }`.
- Annotate the constant as `export const SOURCE_CACHE_LIMITS: SourceCacheLimits = Object.freeze({ maxEntries: 2048, maxBytes: 33_554_432 });`. It stays frozen at runtime; the annotation only stops literal-type inference.
- Type the field as `private readonly limits: SourceCacheLimits;` and the constructor as `constructor(limits: Partial<SourceCacheLimits> = {})`.
- Change nothing else. The runtime validation stays byte-identical: plain-object check, known keys via Object.hasOwn(SOURCE_CACHE_LIMITS, key), positive safe integers, invalidInput fields. So do the LRU and the byte accounting.

(b) In src/context/negativeSearch.test.ts line 215, drop the `as never` cast from `new SourceCache({ maxEntries: 1 } as never)`. It was the workaround for this bug.

(c) In src/context/sourceCache.test.ts, next to C2/C3, add 'C2b accepts custom maxEntries and maxBytes together':
- `const c = new SourceCache({ maxEntries: 1, maxBytes: 10 })` (the DoD's exact call).
- c.set('a', 'x'); c.set('b', 'y'). Expect c.get('a') toBeUndefined and c.get('b') toBe('y').
- c.set('c', 'x'.repeat(20)). It is 22 JSON bytes, over 10. Expect c.get('c') toBeUndefined and c.get('b') still 'y'.

Error handling: the C5 refusal rows stay unchanged and green. Bad limits are still refused at runtime.
implementationPlan.note: Added exported SourceCacheLimits interface, annotated frozen constant, widened field/ctor types; removed as-never cast; added C2b. Runtime validation untouched. 735 other dirty paths are peers' and left alone.
